clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's stroke in June 1991, within two years: your late nights through secondary school, the move to Hollin Road that autumn, your wrist injury stopping your playing in October 1991, your row with Rafe in November and your retreat into radios, your mother filling in your college forms that spring, and your low functioning through 1992; by early 1994, when you stung at your dad not hearing of your film, you had turned a corner and were finding your drive again. Your grandfather's return to the family in 1989 and the household moves sit beside these shifts, with your own trouble building through the period.

clusters.name: Your separation from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Around your bonding with Joelle in early 1998, within two years: your insomnia began that January worsening before concerts; you were playing your best and winning competitions through 1999, yet in July you split up; by August you had started with your therapist, Victor Halloran. The shift in your functioning up sits beside the shifts in your symptom and the separation, all close in those months, and no one else's shifts show then.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within two years: you ran out of steam for performing and were low by the month; you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002 and were done with performing; you grew distant from your parents that autumn; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol that winter and left Gull Harbour to live with her; by October 2003 you split up and sank into a deep depression. You returned to Thornbury and could not face your family, though you relied on friends—Silas, Corbin and Dale took you in. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home that September. The shifts pile up close together through these months, with your functioning falling and your distance from family rising as your grandmother's illness deepened.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you spent four weeks building at Alder Creek in July; you were too drained for a phone call with your mother; she pressed to visit you and the visit went wrong, the door shut on her; you left for nursing school that August and stopped speaking to your mother, a cutoff that held for roughly a year. Your grandfather Clifford also died in January 2008. The shifts in your distance from your mother and the cutoff sit beside these losses, with your functioning pulled down by the months at the lodge.

clusters.name: Wren's family gathering at the lake, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within two years: your sister Tara married James; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis; your aunt Imogen's memory slipped and she grew sharp with your cousin Hal; your job steadied and paid well, yet you began to feel you ought to drive your projects forward; you started a sleeping pill to ease the fretting; you aimed for shorter regular calls with your mother; your sister Tara was expecting her first child. In late October 2019, at Wren's mother Frances's retirement party at the lake house, Wren was swamped and you overfunctioned settling her; her family's fusion—her, her father Hugo, and her brother Leo all in constant talk—pressed on you; you had no sleep from the small hours and could only pull back as the others rose, feeling you did not belong. Within days the anxiety eased once the weekend had a plan. Your anxiety rose and fell with the family gatherings, and your sleep troubles peaked around Wren's family, though the period holds steady gains in your functioning and in your reach toward your mother.
